issues.detail: The Greek 'δυναστης κανδακης' (dynastēs kandakēs) refers to the official/governor of the Queen's 'kandake' (a specific title or royal household role), but the Vietnamese translates it as 'kẻ có quyền thế của Can-đác, nữ vương Ê-thi-ô-bi', which incorrectly identifies 'Can-đác' as a person's name rather than a title/office associated with the Queen.

The Greek 'επι πασης της γαζης αυτης' refers to the 'treasury' or 'wealth' of the Queen. The Vietnamese 'coi sóc mọi kho tàng' (overseeing all treasures) adds a functional action ('coi sóc' - overseeing/taking care of) that is not explicitly in the Greek, which simply identifies him as the official of her treasury.
